tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description explicitly frames when to use the skill ('Use this skill when an endpoint is Failed or never passes its health check...'), focuses on symptoms/user intent (slow, errors, scaling wrong, costs too much) rather than implementation details, and lists many explicit trigger scenarios across real-time, serverless, async, and batch transform contexts. It is fairly long but remains a focused single paragraph covering a genuinely broad domain, so the length is justified by scope rather than being bloated.
tests.evidence: "Use this skill when an endpoint is Failed or never passes its health check, cannot read its model artifact from S3 or KMS, is unreachable from a private subnet, returns ModelError or 5xx, does not scale out, or sits idle while billed; when a serverless endpoint cold-starts or throttles; when async requests never notify, back up or fail on large inputs; when a transform job fails to parse records, times out or reports Completed with records missing..."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body avoids explaining general concepts (e.g., what an endpoint is, what CloudWatch is) and jumps directly into SageMaker-specific checks, APIs, and procedures the agent would not otherwise know (check-id catalog, router table, api-quirks). It is dense but every line carries domain-specific information.
tests.evidence: 'Grounded in checks-sagemaker-inference.md; load it when a symptom matches a row below. Match the symptom, confirm with the collection calls, then report with the check-id and severity from the catalog.'

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The check catalog table and router table are compact indexes (check-id, severity, one-line description) rather than full detailed reference material; the actual detection rules, remediations, and citations are deferred to references/checks-sagemaker-inference.md. No large reference blocks or detailed decision-tree branches are embedded.
tests.evidence: 'Load checks-sagemaker-inference.md before writing any finding: it holds the full detection rules, remediations, and citations.'

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ is linked via markdown link syntax in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is accompanied by specific conditions for loading (e.g., 'load it before assigning any check-id', 'load at Step 5', 'load whenever the user names a specific error or symptom').
tests.evidence: '[api-quirks.md](references/api-quirks.md) — load before interpreting any response that looks clean, empty, InService or Completed'

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths of the form references/filename.md with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, non-negotiable operations (read-only guardrails, account ID masking, severity invention) are stated as strict rules, while flexible areas (how to diagnose a symptom, fit decisions) explain the why and let the agent reason with evidence-based judgment.
tests.evidence: 'Never invent a threshold: a tuning/right-sizing judgment with no AWS-published number is marked workload-specific and reported as INFO, while a binary failed/absent state keeps its catalog severity.'

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where there are multiple serving options (real-time, serverless, async, batch), the skill designates a decision framework (fit decision in Step 4) rather than presenting them as equal menu options, and guides the user to the config/metrics that decide the fit.
tests.evidence: 'Fit decision (one decision, made here). Low or bursty traffic on an always-on real-time endpoint is the idle-cost signal LLM-SM-008. Whether that traffic belongs on serverless... or async... is LLM-SM-SERVE-005, driven by payload size and invocation duration.'

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable procedure (Review Procedure steps 1-8, router table matching symptom patterns to checks) that applies across any endpoint/job, rather than a one-off declaration for a specific resource.
tests.evidence: 'Run the steps in order and track progress against this checklist. Each step depends on state gathered by the one before it, and each branches by area: run only the branches for the areas in scope.'

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has an extensive 'Common wrong answers' section plus an 'Error Handling' section documenting non-obvious API quirks and misleading responses, which function as gotchas.
tests.evidence: '"The endpoint is InService, so it's serving traffic and the queue is fine." InService is control-plane state; a real-time, async or serverless variant can be InService with CurrentInstanceCount = 0...'

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill explicitly provides templates for its three report types, referenced in assets/.
tests.evidence: '[endpoint-health-report-template.md](assets/endpoint-health-report-template.md) — load when a full real-time endpoint report is requested.'

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline templates exist in the body; templates are stored in assets/ and referenced conditionally.
tests.evidence: Body contains no inline report template skeleton; templates are only linked, e.g. '[endpoint-health-report-template.md](assets/endpoint-health-report-template.md)'.

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All three asset files are linked in the body (Step 8 section and Appendix).

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each asset link specifies the condition under which it should be loaded (full report requested, for a specific area).
tests.evidence: '[batch-job-health-report-template.md](assets/batch-job-health-report-template.md) — load when a full batch transform report is requested.'

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: All asset references use relative paths of the form assets/filename.md.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The Review Procedure is presented as a checkbox checklist with Step N format, and the detailed sections below use matching '### Step N — ...' headings that reference the same step numbers.
tests.evidence: '- [ ] Step 1: Identify the area and enumerate resources.' ... '### Step 1 — Identify the area'

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit 'Before You Present — Validate Your Own Output' section with a checklist to verify findings before presenting, matching the do-work-then-check pattern.
tests.evidence: 'A wrong or unsupported finding is worse than a slow one. Before presenting, re-check your output against this list. Treat it as a gate, not a suggestion.'
